causal_assumptions.consistency: Naloxone and comparison conditions follow the reported protocol.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Depends on the source allocation and blinding procedures.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Relevant protocol groups received antagonist and comparison conditions.

claims.causal_estimand: Effect of naloxone versus control treatment on expectation-induced placebo analgesia in the study protocol.

confidence.rationale: Pharmacological perturbation directly tests opioid-receptor involvement, but allocation details and a standardized effect were not extracted.

limitations: Antagonist blockade identifies receptor involvement more directly than a full psychological or neural mechanism.

boundary_conditions: Does not establish that every placebo analgesic response is opioid-mediated.
scope.population: Participants in the Amanzio and Benedetti human experimental ischemic arm-pain study.

claims.statement: In the Amanzio and Benedetti ischemic-pain experiment, naloxone administration eliminated placebo analgesia induced by expectation cues.
claims.temporal_ordering: Expectation induction and naloxone administration preceded pain assessment.

causal_assumptions.consistency: Medication groups received the reported pharmacological protocols.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Participants were allocated across all medication groups.

claims.causal_estimand: Between-group effect of sulpiride or L-dopa versus placebo on later placebo analgesia.

confidence.rationale: A double-blind randomized placebo-controlled experiment used opposing pharmacological manipulations and combined frequentist and Bayesian analyses.

limitations: The result constrains a direct causal role under the tested dose

boundary_conditions: A null protocol effect does not prove dopamine is irrelevant to every placebo process or population.
scope.population: 168 healthy volunteers in the registered experiment.
scope.temporal_scope: Expectation formation during conditioning and placebo analgesia one day later.

claims.statement: In Kunkel et al., randomized sulpiride or L-dopa did not detectably alter formation of positive treatment expectation or placebo analgesia one day later relative to placebo medication.
claims.temporal_ordering: Medication preceded conditioning; pain outcomes were assessed one day later.

confidence.rationale: Individual-participant meta-analysis increases precision, but statistical mediation of fMRI measures does not identify causal neural mediation.

indirect_effect.notes: The abstract reports mediation through multiple increased and decreased regional activity measures.

limitations: The NPS is one measured component of a broader reported mediator set and is not the mechanism itself.

boundary_conditions: The mediator set and indirect effects are model-dependent and do not establish necessity or sufficiency.
scope.population: 409 participants from 16 within-participant placebo neuroimaging studies.
scope.temporal_scope: Pain-period activity and analgesic response in suggestion-only and conditioning-plus-suggestion conditions.

claims.statement: Across the Placebo Imaging Consortium dataset, greater analgesia from conditioning plus suggestion versus suggestion alone was statistically mediated by changes in specified cortical, striatal, sensory-nociceptive, and cerebellar activity.
claims.temporal_ordering: Protocol induction preceded pain-period imaging and pain-response estimation; within-trial mediator-outcome ordering remains limited.

confidence.rationale: Naloxone blockade supports opioid involvement, while protocol heterogeneity and nonopioid conditioned effects argue against a universal pathway.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The hypothesis is weakened if adequately powered receptor blockade repeatedly leaves expectation-induced placebo analgesia unchanged under matched protocols.
limitations: This integrative mechanism claim is narrower than saying that expectation is sufficient or that all placebo analgesia is opioid-mediated.

boundary_conditions: Conditioning with nonopioid drugs can produce naloxone-insensitive placebo responses.
scope.population: Humans in experimental placebo analgesia paradigms represented by the included pharmacological study.
scope.temporal_scope: Expectation induction through subsequent experimental pain assessment.

claims.statement: Positive treatment expectation may recruit endogenous opioid signaling that contributes to reduced pain responding in some placebo protocols.
claims.temporal_ordering: Positive treatment expectation is induced before the pain outcome.

evidence.design: Human ischemic arm-pain experiment crossing expectation or drug-conditioning procedures with naloxone challenge.

effect.notes: Expectation-cue placebo responses were reported as completely blocked by naloxone.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract, expectation-cue and naloxone result.
limitations: and numerical effect were not extracted from the abstract.
evidence.population: Participants in a human experimental ischemic arm-pain protocol; sample size not extracted from the abstract.
evidence.summary: Opioid-receptor antagonism removed the expectation-cue placebo response in this protocol.

evidence.design: Pharmacological dissociation across expectation, morphine conditioning, and ketorolac conditioning procedures.

effect.notes: Responses ranged from reversible to partially reversible to insensitive depending on procedure.

limitations: Pharmacological dissociation does not by itself identify the complete intervening pathway.
evidence.population: Participants in the human experimental ischemic arm-pain study.
evidence.summary: Differential naloxone sensitivity supports multiple protocol-dependent implementations rather than one universal placebo mechanism.

evidence.design: Registered double-blind randomized placebo-controlled between-subject trial of sulpiride, L-dopa, and placebo.

effect.metric: medication-group effect on expectation and placebo analgesia
effect.notes: Frequentist and Bayesian analyses supported no direct effect under the tested protocol.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract, randomized medication contrast and day-1 outcome.
evidence.summary: Opposing dopamine manipulations did not alter treatment-expectation formation or next-day placebo analgesia.

evidence.design: Individual-participant meta-analysis of 16 within-participant placebo fMRI studies comparing suggestion alone with suggestion plus conditioning.

effect.metric: statistical indirect effects through brain-activity measures
effect.notes: Increased prefrontal and striatal and decreased sensory-nociceptive and cerebellar activity were reported.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract, individual-participant meta-analysis and mediation result.
limitations: Study heterogeneity and mediator-outcome causal assumptions remain.
evidence.summary: Conditioning added analgesia and distinct neural associations, with reported statistical mediation across pooled participant data.
